parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct; a 2010 anti-discrimination law covers goods, services, housing and health care, and a 2013 hate-crime provision covers gender identity. But enforcement is documented as slow and bureaucratically impeded (one of nine complaints concluded; a lawmaker's 'homosexuality is a disease' remark drew a reprimand only after nine months), and the record shows symbolic regression (2016 removal of SO/GI from Article 18) plus hostile social attitudes (9.3% would accept an LGBT family doctor; majority would not want homosexual neighbours). Crucially, nothing documents a traveller-facing exposure: no border rejections, facility bans, custody rule, or police targeting of trans visitors. The ten logged bias cases are a raw count with no denominator, so violence is treated as undocumented. This sits at the 'elevated, repeated friction with incomplete remedy' level rather than the universal-exposure tier.
